+/**
+ * SDD section 16 and section 32. Checks out the organization skills repository and makes it
+ * read-only. It lives in its own directory, not under `reference/`, so it can never collide with
+ * a reference repository name, and it never appears in the reference path list of the prompt.
+ */
+export const checkoutOrganizationSkills = async (
+  sandbox: Sandbox,
+  ref: SandboxRef,
+  spec: RepositorySpec,
+): Promise<CheckedOutRepository> => {
+  const path = `${ref.workspacePath}/organization-skills`;
+  const baseSha = await clone(sandbox, ref, spec, path);
+  // SDD section 29 denies writing a repository the agent must only read. This is a file mode.
+  await run(sandbox, ref, { file: "chmod", args: ["-R", "a-w", path] });
+  return { url: spec.url, path, baseSha, readOnly: true };
+};
+
 /** The whole SDD section 32 checkout, for a caller that needs no step between the two halves. */

$ cd /Users/nathananderson-tennant/Development/factoree && cat > /tmp/check-skills.mjs <<'EOF'
import { resolveSkills, MAX_SKILLS } from "./src/domain/runs/skill-discovery.ts";

const origin = (overrides = {}) => ({
  scope: "repository",
  root: "/w/primary",
  directory: ".agents/skills",
  name: "fastify-routes",
  path: "/w/primary/.agents/skills/fastify-routes/SKILL.md",
  ...overrides,
});
const skill = (name, over = {}) => ({
  name,
  description: `the ${name} skill`,
  origin: origin({ name, path: `/w/primary/.agents/skills/${name}/SKILL.md`, ...over }),
});

const repositorySkills = Array.from({ length: MAX_SKILLS }, (_v, index) =>
  skill(`zzz-repo-${String(index).padStart(3, "0")}`, { scope: "repository" }),
);
const organizationSkills = Array.from({ length: 5 }, (_v, index) =>
  skill(`aaa-org-${String(index).padStart(3, "0")}`, {
    scope: "organization",
    root: "/w/organization-skills",
    path: `/w/organization-skills/.agents/skills/aaa-org-${String(index).padStart(3, "0")}/SKILL.md`,
  }),
);
const set = resolveSkills([...repositorySkills, ...organizationSkills]);
console.log("skills length", set.skills.length);
console.log("scopes", set.skills.map(e => e.origin.scope).join(","));
console.log("every repo?", set.skills.every((entry) => entry.origin.scope === "repository"));
console.log("dropped", set.droppedForLimit);
EOF

export const resolveSkills = (candidates: DiscoveredSkill[]): SkillSet => {
  const applied = new Map<string, DiscoveredSkill>();
  const shadowed = new Map<string, SkillOrigin[]>();

  for (const candidate of candidates) {
    const existing = applied.get(candidate.name);
    if (existing === undefined) {
      applied.set(candidate.name, candidate);
      continue;
    }
    shadowed.set(candidate.name, [...(shadowed.get(candidate.name) ?? []), candidate.origin]);
  }

  // The cap must apply in precedence order, not alphabetical order. `applied` still holds its
  // entries in insertion order, which is precedence order, so slicing it here keeps a repository
  // skill over an organization skill even when the organization name sorts first. The alphabetical
  // sort applies only after the cap, for the rendered output.
  const precedenceOrdered = [...applied.values()];
  const kept = precedenceOrdered.slice(0, MAX_SKILLS).sort((left, right) => left.name.localeCompare(right.name));

  const conflicts: SkillConflict[] = [];
  for (const entry of kept) {
    const others = shadowed.get(entry.name);
    if (others === undefined || others.length === 0) continue;
    conflicts.push({ name: entry.name, applied: entry.origin, shadowed: others });
  }

  return {
    skills: kept,
    conflicts,

+/**
+ * The largest number of bytes this reader loads from one `SKILL.md`. `parseSkillDocument` reads
+ * only the YAML frontmatter, which sits at the top of the document, so a bound this size never
+ * loses a real frontmatter. It stops an oversized file from exhausting memory.
+ */
+export const SKILL_FILE_READ_CAP_BYTES = 65536;
+
+/** A line the reader emits when a directory listing fails for a reason other than "missing". */
+export interface SkillSourceLogger {
+  warn: (message: string, detail: { path: string; exitCode: number; stderr: string }) => void;
+}
+
+const NO_LOGGER: SkillSourceLogger = { warn: () => {} };
+
+/**
+ * True when `stderr` names an ordinary missing path. `ls` and `head` both write this message for
+ * a path that simply does not exist, on every platform this project targets. Any other failure,
+ * for example a permission error, is unexpected and is worth one log line.
+ */
+const namesAMissingPath = (stderr: string): boolean => /no such file or directory/i.test(stderr);

$ cd /Users/nathananderson-tennant/Development/factoree && echo "=== HEAD skill-discovery.ts resolveSkills ===" && git show HEAD:src/domain/runs/skill-discovery.ts | sed -n '99,140p'
=== HEAD skill-discovery.ts resolveSkills ===
/**
 * Applies the precedence order of the candidate list and reports every conflict. The caller
 * supplies the candidates already ordered, so this function never re-orders them. It applies the
 * first candidate of each name and records every later candidate of that name as shadowed.
 *
 * SDD section 16 forbids a silent overwrite. A shadowed skill is therefore kept, named, and
 * reported. Nothing is discarded without a line that says so.
 */
export const resolveSkills = (candidates: DiscoveredSkill[]): SkillSet => {
  const applied = new Map<string, DiscoveredSkill>();
  const shadowed = new Map<string, SkillOrigin[]>();

  for (const candidate of candidates) {
    const existing = applied.get(candidate.name);
    if (existing === undefined) {
      applied.set(candidate.name, candidate);
      continue;
    }
    shadowed.set(candidate.name, [...(shadowed.get(candidate.name) ?? []), candidate.origin]);
  }

  const sorted = [...applied.values()].sort((left, right) => left.name.localeCompare(right.name));
  const kept = sorted.slice(0, MAX_SKILLS);
  const keptNames = new Set(kept.map((entry) => entry.name));

  const conflicts: SkillConflict[] = [];
  for (const entry of kept) {
    const others = shadowed.get(entry.name);
    if (others === undefined || others.length === 0) continue;
    conflicts.push({ name: entry.name, applied: entry.origin, shadowed: others });
  }

  return {
    skills: kept,
    conflicts,
    droppedForLimit: sorted.length - keptNames.size,
  };
};

const scopeWord = (scope: SkillScope): string =>
  scope === "repository" ? "repository skill" : "organization skill";

    const many = Array.from({ length: MAX_SKILLS + 5 }, (_value, index) =>
      skill(`skill-${String(index).padStart(3, "0")}`),
    );
    const set = resolveSkills(many);
    expect(set.skills).toHaveLength(MAX_SKILLS);

describe("renderSkillLines", () => {
  it("reports no skill as one plain line", () => {
    expect(renderSkillLines({ skills: [], conflicts: [], droppedForLimit: 0 })).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("names the skill, the description, the scope, and the path", () => {
    const lines = renderSkillLines(resolveSkills([skill("routes")]));
    expect(lines[0]).toBe(
      "routes — the routes skill (repository skill, /w/primary/.agents/skills/routes/SKILL.md)",
    );
  });

  it("states a name conflict, the applied path, and every ignored path", () => {
    const set = resolveSkills([
      skill("routes"),
      {
        name: "routes",
        description: "the organization version",
        origin: origin({ scope: "organization", root: "/w/organization-skills", name: "routes",
          path: "/w/organization-skills/.agents/skills/routes/SKILL.md" }),
      },
    ]);
    const lines = renderSkillLines(set);
    expect(lines.some((line) => line.startsWith("Name conflict: \"routes\""))).toBe(true);
    expect(lines.some((line) => line.includes("/w/organization-skills/.agents/skills/routes/SKILL.md"))).toBe(true);
  });

  it("states the number of skills it dropped for the limit", () => {
    const many = Array.from({ length: MAX_SKILLS + 2 }, (_value, index) =>
      skill(`skill-${String(index).padStart(3, "0")}`),
    );
    const lines = renderSkillLines(resolveSkills(many));
    expect(lines.some((line) => line.includes("2 further skills"))).toBe(true);
  });
});

import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { NetworkPolicyNotEnforcedError } from "~/domain/runs/sandbox.js";
import { SandboxManager } from "~/domain/runs/sandbox-manager.js";
import { RunConfigurationError } from "~/domain/runs/run-configuration-error.js";
import { DEFAULT_PROJECT_DEFAULTS } from "~/domain/runs/project-runtime-config.js";
import { FakeSandbox } from "../support/fake-sandbox.js";

const HEAD = "aaaabbbbccccddddeeeeffff0000111122223333";

const DEFAULT_CONFIG_YAML =
  "version: 1\nverify:\n  commands:\n    - name: test\n      run: npm test\n" +
  "sandbox:\n  allowedDomains:\n    - registry.npmjs.org\n";

const BOOTSTRAP_CONFIG_YAML =
  "version: 1\nbootstrap:\n  command: npm ci\nverify:\n  commands:\n    - name: test\n      run: npm test\n" +
  "sandbox:\n  allowedDomains:\n    - registry.npmjs.org\n";

interface Scripted {
  matcher: RegExp;
  result: Partial<{ exitCode: number; stdout: string; stderr: string }>;
}

/**
 * Builds a `FakeSandbox` that serves `yaml` for `.factoree/config.yaml`, a fixed commit SHA for
 * `git rev-parse HEAD`, and every other command as a success, unless `overrides` matches first.
 */
const sandboxWithConfig = (
  yaml: string,
  overrides: Scripted[] = [],
  capabilities?: ConstructorParameters<typeof FakeSandbox>[0],
): FakeSandbox => {
  const sandbox = capabilities === undefined ? new FakeSandbox() : new FakeSandbox(capabilities);
  sandbox.onExec = (command) => {
    const last = command.args[command.args.length - 1] ?? "";
    if (command.file === "cat" && last.endsWith(".factoree/config.yaml")) {
      return { exitCode: 0, stdout: yaml, stderr: "" };
    }
    if (command.file === "cat") return { exitCode: 1, stdout: "", stderr: "no such file" };
    const line = [command.file, ...command.args].join(" ");
    const scripted = overrides.find((entry) => entry.matcher.test(line));
    if (scripted !== undefined) {
      return { exitCode: 0, stdout: "", stderr: "", ...scripted.result };
    }
    if (command.file === "git" && command.args.includes("rev-parse")) {
      return { exitCode: 0, stdout: `${HEAD}\n`, stderr: "" };
    }
    return { exitCode: 0, stdout: "", stderr: "" };
  };
  return sandbox;
};

/**
 * Wraps the `onExec` of a fake sandbox, so `ls` answers a directory listing and `cat` answers a
 * `SKILL.md`. Every other command falls through to the wrapped hook.
 */
const withSkillFiles = (
  sandbox: FakeSandbox,
  listings: Record<string, string[]>,
  files: Record<string, string>,
): FakeSandbox => {
  const base = sandbox.onExec;
  sandbox.onExec = (command) => {
    const last = command.args[command.args.length - 1] ?? "";
    if (command.file === "ls") {
      const entries = listings[last];
      if (entries === undefined) return { exitCode: 1, stdout: "", stderr: "no such directory" };
      return { exitCode: 0, stdout: `${entries.join("\n")}\n`, stderr: "" };
    }
    const body = files[last];
    if (command.file === "cat" && body !== undefined) return { exitCode: 0, stdout: body, stderr: "" };
    return base === null ? { exitCode: 0, stdout: "", stderr: "" } : base(command);
  };
  return sandbox;
};

const input = {
  runId: "run-1",
  tenantId: "tenant-1",
  projectId: "project-1",
  primary: { url: "https://github.com/acme/app.git", ref: "main" },
  references: [],
  defaults: DEFAULT_PROJECT_DEFAULTS,
};

describe("SandboxManager.prepare", () => {
  it("follows the SDD section 32 order: create, network policy, checkout, bootstrap, checkpoint", async () => {
    const sandbox = sandboxWithConfig(BOOTSTRAP_CONFIG_YAML);
    const manager = new SandboxManager({ sandbox });
    await manager.prepare(input);
    const order = sandbox.calls.filter(
      (call) => call === "create" || call === "applyNetworkPolicy" || call.startsWith("checkpoint"),
    );
    expect(order).toEqual([
      "create",
      "applyNetworkPolicy",
      "applyNetworkPolicy",
      "applyNetworkPolicy",
      "checkpoint:baseline",
    ]);
  });

  it("applies the network policy before it runs any command", async () => {
    const sandbox = sandboxWithConfig(DEFAULT_CONFIG_YAML);
    const manager = new SandboxManager({ sandbox });
    await manager.prepare(input);
    const policyIndex = sandbox.calls.indexOf("applyNetworkPolicy");
    const firstExec = sandbox.calls.findIndex((call) => call.startsWith("exec:"));
    expect(policyIndex).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
    expect(policyIndex).toBeLessThan(firstExec);
  });

  it("creates the workspace directory after the policy and before the first clone", async () => {
    const sandbox = sandboxWithConfig(DEFAULT_CONFIG_YAML);
    const manager = new SandboxManager({ sandbox });
    await manager.prepare(input);
    const policyIndex = sandbox.calls.indexOf("applyNetworkPolicy");
    const mkdirIndex = sandbox.commands.findIndex(
      (command) => command.file === "mkdir" && command.args.includes("/workspace"),
    );
    const cloneIndex = sandbox.commands.findIndex(
      (command) => command.file === "git" && command.args[0] === "clone",
    );
    expect(mkdirIndex).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
    expect(cloneIndex).toBeGreaterThan(mkdirIndex);
    // The applyNetworkPolicy call is not in `commands`, so compare against the raw call order.
    const mkdirCallIndex = sandbox.calls.indexOf("exec:mkdir");
    expect(mkdirCallIndex).toBeGreaterThan(policyIndex);
  });

  it("passes the configured allow list to the last network policy", async () => {
    const sandbox = sandboxWithConfig(DEFAULT_CONFIG_YAML);
    const manager = new SandboxManager({ sandbox });
    await manager.prepare(input);
    expect(sandbox.policies.at(-1)).toEqual({ allowedDomains: ["registry.npmjs.org"] });
  });

  it("runs the bootstrap command in the primary worktree after the checkout", async () => {
    const sandbox = sandboxWithConfig(BOOTSTRAP_CONFIG_YAML);
    const manager = new SandboxManager({ sandbox });
    await manager.prepare(input);
    const bootstrap = sandbox.commands.find((command) => command.args.includes("npm ci"));
    expect(bootstrap?.cwd).toBe("/workspace/primary");
  });

  it("skips bootstrap when the repository configures no bootstrap command", async () => {
    const sandbox = sandboxWithConfig(DEFAULT_CONFIG_YAML);
    const manager = new SandboxManager({ sandbox });
    await manager.prepare(input);
    expect(sandbox.commands.some((command) => command.args.includes("npm ci"))).toBe(false);
  });

  it("fails the preparation when the bootstrap command fails", async () => {
    const sandbox = sandboxWithConfig(BOOTSTRAP_CONFIG_YAML, [
      { matcher: /npm ci/, result: { exitCode: 1, stderr: "install failed" } },
    ]);
    const manager = new SandboxManager({ sandbox });
    await expect(manager.prepare(input)).rejects.toThrow(/install failed/);
  });

  it("reports a failed bootstrap command as a configuration fault", async () => {
    // SDD section 49. The command comes from the repository configuration, so a retry repeats it.
    const sandbox = sandboxWithConfig(BOOTSTRAP_CONFIG_YAML, [
      { matcher: /npm ci/, result: { exitCode: 1, stderr: "install failed" } },
    ]);
    const manager = new SandboxManager({ sandbox });
    await expect(manager.prepare(input)).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(RunConfigurationError);
  });

  it("destroys the sandbox when preparation fails, so no sandbox leaks", async () => {
    const sandbox = sandboxWithConfig(DEFAULT_CONFIG_YAML, [
      { matcher: /clone/, result: { exitCode: 128, stderr: "clone failed" } },
    ]);
    const manager = new SandboxManager({ sandbox });
    await expect(manager.prepare(input)).rejects.toThrow(/clone failed/);
    expect(sandbox.destroyed).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it("returns the sandbox reference, the base SHA, and the baseline checkpoint", async () => {
    const sandbox = sandboxWithConfig(DEFAULT_CONFIG_YAML);
    const manager = new SandboxManager({ sandbox });
    const prepared = await manager.prepare(input);
    expect(prepared.ref.id).toContain("run-1");
    expect(prepared.checkout.primary.baseSha).toBe(HEAD);
    expect(prepared.baselineCheckpoint?.name).toBe("baseline");
  });

  it("refuses a sandbox that cannot enforce the network policy", async () => {
    const sandbox = new FakeSandbox({
      enforcesNetworkPolicy: false,
      supportsCheckpoints: true,
      supportsExposedServices: false,
    });
    const manager = new SandboxManager({ sandbox });
    await expect(manager.prepare(input)).rejects.toThrow(NetworkPolicyNotEnforcedError);
  });

  it("accepts an unenforced sandbox only when the caller opts in", async () => {
    const sandbox = sandboxWithConfig(DEFAULT_CONFIG_YAML, [], {
      enforcesNetworkPolicy: false,
      supportsCheckpoints: true,
      supportsExposedServices: false,
    });
    const manager = new SandboxManager({ sandbox, allowUnenforcedNetwork: true });
    await expect(manager.prepare(input)).resolves.toBeDefined();
  });

  it("skips the checkpoint when the adapter does not support checkpoints", async () => {
    const sandbox = sandboxWithConfig(DEFAULT_CONFIG_YAML, [], {
      enforcesNetworkPolicy: true,
      supportsCheckpoints: false,
      supportsExposedServices: false,
    });
    const manager = new SandboxManager({ sandbox });
    const prepared = await manager.prepare(input);
    expect(prepared.baselineCheckpoint).toBeNull();
    expect(sandbox.checkpoints).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  it("gives two Runs two different sandbox identifiers", async () => {
    const sandbox = sandboxWithConfig(DEFAULT_CONFIG_YAML);
    const manager = new SandboxManager({ sandbox });
    const first = await manager.prepare(input);
    const second = await manager.prepare({ ...input, runId: "run-2" });
    expect(first.ref.id).not.toBe(second.ref.id);
  });

  it("destroys the sandbox on release", async () => {
    const sandbox = sandboxWithConfig(DEFAULT_CONFIG_YAML);
    const manager = new SandboxManager({ sandbox });
    const prepared = await manager.prepare(input);
    await manager.release(prepared);
    expect(sandbox.destroyed).toContain(prepared.ref.id);
  });
});

describe("repository configuration and staged network policy", () => {
  const configYaml =
    "version: 1\nverify:\n  commands:\n    - name: test\n      run: npm test\n" +
    "sandbox:\n  allowedDomains:\n    - registry.npmjs.org\n";

  const sandboxServing = (yaml: string | null): FakeSandbox => {
    const sandbox = new FakeSandbox();
    sandbox.onExec = (command) => {
      const last = command.args[command.args.length - 1] ?? "";
      if (command.file === "cat" && last.endsWith(".factoree/config.yaml")) {
        return yaml === null
          ? { exitCode: 1, stdout: "", stderr: "no such file" }
          : { exitCode: 0, stdout: yaml, stderr: "" };
      }
      if (command.file === "cat") return { exitCode: 1, stdout: "", stderr: "no such file" };
      if (command.file === "git" && command.args.includes("rev-parse")) {
        return { exitCode: 0, stdout: `${HEAD}\n`, stderr: "" };
      }
      return { exitCode: 0, stdout: "", stderr: "" };
    };
    return sandbox;
  };

  const prepare = (sandbox: FakeSandbox) =>
    new SandboxManager({ sandbox }).prepare({
      runId: "run-1",
      tenantId: "tenant-1",
      projectId: "project-1",
      primary: { url: "https://git.test/owner/app.git", ref: "main" },
      references: [],
      defaults: { stagingRead: false, spriteRetentionHours: 24 },
    });

  it("applies three policies and never runs the agent under a wider one", async () => {
    const sandbox = sandboxServing(configYaml);
    const prepared = await prepare(sandbox);
    expect(sandbox.networkPolicies).toEqual([
      { allowedDomains: ["git.test"] },
      { allowedDomains: ["git.test", "registry.npmjs.org"] },
      { allowedDomains: ["registry.npmjs.org"] },
    ]);
    expect(prepared.runtime.allowedDomains).toEqual(["registry.npmjs.org"]);
    expect(prepared.verifyCommands).toEqual([{ name: "test", run: "npm test" }]);
  });

  it("applies the last policy immediately before the baseline checkpoint", async () => {
    const sandbox = sandboxServing(configYaml);
    await prepare(sandbox);
    const ordered = sandbox.calls.filter(
      (call) => call === "applyNetworkPolicy" || call.startsWith("checkpoint"),
    );
    expect(ordered.at(-1)).toBe("checkpoint:baseline");
    expect(ordered.at(-2)).toBe("applyNetworkPolicy");
  });

  it("fails with a configuration error when the repository has no config file", async () => {
    await expect(prepare(sandboxServing(null))).rejects.toThrow(RunConfigurationError);
  });

  it("destroys the sandbox when the configuration is missing", async () => {
    const sandbox = sandboxServing(null);
    await expect(prepare(sandbox)).rejects.toThrow(RunConfigurationError);
    expect(sandbox.calls).toContain("destroy");
  });

  it("returns the repository instructions it found", async () => {
    const sandbox = new FakeSandbox();
    sandbox.onExec = (command) => {
      const last = command.args[command.args.length - 1] ?? "";
      if (command.file === "git" && command.args.includes("rev-parse")) {
        return { exitCode: 0, stdout: `${HEAD}\n`, stderr: "" };
      }
      if (command.file !== "cat") return { exitCode: 0, stdout: "", stderr: "" };
      if (last.endsWith(".factoree/config.yaml")) return { exitCode: 0, stdout: configYaml, stderr: "" };
      if (last.endsWith("AGENTS.md")) return { exitCode: 0, stdout: "house rules\n", stderr: "" };
      return { exitCode: 1, stdout: "", stderr: "no such file" };
    };
    expect((await prepare(sandbox)).repositoryInstructions).toBe("house rules\n");
  });

  it("runs the bootstrap command between policy two and policy three", async () => {
    // Every other test in this block configures no bootstrap command, so the SDD section 32
    // order test filters the bootstrap exec out of its comparison array. This test proves the
    // bootstrap command itself runs strictly between the second and the third policy: after the
    // reference checkouts can reach the configured allow list, and before the Implementer runs
    // under the narrowed final policy.
    const bootstrapConfigYaml =
      "version: 1\nbootstrap:\n  command: npm ci\nverify:\n  commands:\n    - name: test\n      run: npm test\n" +
      "sandbox:\n  allowedDomains:\n    - registry.npmjs.org\n";
    const sandbox = sandboxServing(bootstrapConfigYaml);
    await prepare(sandbox);
    const policyIndexes = sandbox.calls
      .map((call, index) => ({ call, index }))
      .filter((entry) => entry.call === "applyNetworkPolicy")
      .map((entry) => entry.index);
    expect(policyIndexes).toHaveLength(3);
    const bootstrapIndex = sandbox.calls.indexOf("exec:sh");
    expect(bootstrapIndex).toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    expect(bootstrapIndex).toBeGreaterThan(policyIndexes[1] ?? -1);
    expect(bootstrapIndex).toBeLessThan(policyIndexes[2] ?? -1);
  });

  it("joins a reference repository host into policy one and policy two, and drops it from policy three", async () => {
    // Every other test in this block passes no reference repository, so the host union of
    // policy two is exercised with one host only. This test adds a reference repository on a
    // host distinct from the primary one, and proves both hosts reach policy one and policy
    // two, and neither reaches policy three, which carries the configured allow list alone.
    const sandbox = sandboxServing(configYaml);
    await new SandboxManager({ sandbox }).prepare({
      runId: "run-1",
      tenantId: "tenant-1",
      projectId: "project-1",
      primary: { url: "https://git.test/owner/app.git", ref: "main" },
      references: [{ url: "https://other.test/owner/design.git", ref: "main" }],
      defaults: { stagingRead: false, spriteRetentionHours: 24 },
    });
    expect(sandbox.networkPolicies).toEqual([
      { allowedDomains: ["git.test", "other.test"] },
      { allowedDomains: ["git.test", "other.test", "registry.npmjs.org"] },
      { allowedDomains: ["registry.npmjs.org"] },
    ]);
  });
});

describe("SandboxManager.prepare skills", () => {
  it("returns the discovered skill lines of the primary checkout", async () => {
    const sandbox = withSkillFiles(
      sandboxWithConfig(DEFAULT_CONFIG_YAML),
      { "/workspace/primary/.agents/skills": ["routes"] },
      {
        "/workspace/primary/.agents/skills/routes/SKILL.md":
          "---\nname: routes\ndescription: Add a route.\n---\n",
      },
    );
    const manager = new SandboxManager({ sandbox, allowUnenforcedNetwork: true });
    const prepared = await manager.prepare(input);
    expect(prepared.skills.some((line) => line.startsWith("routes — Add a route."))).toBe(true);
  });

  it("returns no skill line for a repository that defines none", async () => {
    const sandbox = withSkillFiles(sandboxWithConfig(DEFAULT_CONFIG_YAML), {}, {});
    const manager = new SandboxManager({ sandbox, allowUnenforcedNetwork: true });
    const prepared = await manager.prepare(input);
    expect(prepared.skills).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("checks out the organization skills repository when the Project names one", async () => {
    const sandbox = sandboxWithConfig(DEFAULT_CONFIG_YAML);
    const manager = new SandboxManager({ sandbox, allowUnenforcedNetwork: true });
    await manager.prepare({
      ...input,
      organizationSkills: { url: "https://git.acme.example/acme/skills.git", ref: "main" },
    });
    expect(sandbox.commands.some((command) => command.args.includes("/workspace/organization-skills"))).toBe(
      true,
    );
    // The first policy must already allow the skills host, because the checkout runs under it.
    expect(sandbox.networkPolicies[0]?.allowedDomains).toContain("git.acme.example");
  });
});

I have completed my review. Here is the audit report.

---

## Phase 11 audit: ClaudeCodeRunner and skill discovery (84a0e9b..HEAD)

I read SDD sections 14, 15, 16, 29, 30, 32, 33, 34, 35, 38, 40, 55, 56, 57, 61, 64 (AT-14/15/37), and 69, and every changed file. Three findings follow.

---

FINDING 1
Category: 1 (skill discovery) — also a correctness defect (category 9)
File: src/domain/runs/skill-discovery.ts:120-121
SDD reference: 16 and 64 (AT-37)
What is wrong: `resolveSkills` sorts the applied skills alphabetically *before* applying the `MAX_SKILLS` cap, then slices. The documented precedence — "a repository skill always precedes an organization skill" — is therefore broken by the cap: an organization skill whose name sorts earlier displaces a repository skill. Because conflicts are only emitted for `kept` skills, a name conflict whose name sorts beyond the cap is dropped with no conflict line, only an anonymous count.
Why it matters: The code's own contract (and the "no silent overwrite / origin recorded" intent of SDD section 16 and AT-37) is violated whenever a repository and an organization skill collide on a late-sorting name or when more than 50 skills exist.
How to reproduce or confirm: `resolveSkills([...50 skills named "zzz-repo-000".."zzz-repo-049" (scope repository), ...5 skills named "aaa-org-000".."aaa-org-004" (scope organization)])` returns `kept` = 5 organization skills + 45 repository skills, so 5 repository skills lose their place to organization skills. The committed test `tests/unit/skill-discovery.test.ts` "caps the applied skills..." uses uniform names, so it never exercises this.

FINDING 2
Category: 9 (correctness) — resource leak
File: src/adapters/runners/cli-agent-runner.ts:59
SDD reference: correctness
What is wrong: The `sessions` map receives one entry per `run`/`resume` and is never pruned; nothing ever calls `this.sessions.delete(...)`. Over a long-lived worker this grows without bound, and each `LiveSession` retains its `Sandbox`, `SandboxRef`, and `ProcessRef`. The comment at lines 53-58 calls this "bounded growth", which is inaccurate — it is unbounded.
Why it matters: Memory grows monotonically for the lifetime of the worker process, which is a real leak, and the misleading comment hides it from future maintainers.
How to reproduce or confirm: A worker that serves N Runs holds N `LiveSession` entries; `activeByRun` is cleaned in the `finally` of `run`, but `sessions` is not, so a monotonic increase is observable across runs with no deletion path.

FINDING 3
Category: 10 (test integrity)
File: tests/acceptance/phase-11-exit.test.ts:32-36
SDD reference: correctness (test proof)
What is wrong: The test "names both required adapters of SDD section 33 in the worker registry" reads `src/bin/worker.ts` as text and asserts it contains the two constructor strings. This proves nothing about runtime behavior: it would pass if the runners were registered but non-functional, or if the constructor strings appeared in a comment or dead code. It claims to verify registration but only greps source text. The companion test at lines 38-44 compares two test files as text, which is likewise a source-text assertion, not a behavioral one.
Why it matters: The phase exit condition (SDD section 69: "the same fixture workflow works with either required runner") is carried by tests 1 and 2, but these two tests assert on source text and deliver no behavioral proof, so they can pass for the wrong reason.
How to reproduce or confirm: Change `worker.ts` to `const runners = new AgentRunnerRegistry([])` while leaving the two `new OpenCodeRunner(...)`/`new ClaudeCodeRunner(...)` strings anywhere in the file; the test still passes even though no runner is registered.

---

Category 2 (organization skills scoped to Project): no finding. `organizationSkillsRepository` lives on the `Project` table and `ProjectRecord`, not on any repository file.
Category 3 (ClaudeCodeRunner AgentRunner port): no finding. `run`, `resume`, and `cancel` implement the port correctly; `resume` correctly resolves `session.processId` and the parsed session id.
Category 4 (prompt/credential on command line / process listing / log): no finding. The `sh -c` script is a constant; the prompt travels only via `FACTOREE_PROMPT` in the environment and is piped via `printf %s "$FACTOREE_PROMPT"`, which is correctly quoted (no `%`-format or shell-injection risk).
Category 5 (output-parser correctness): no finding. The parser is defensive (try/catch per line, `safeParse` guard), returns the correct session id (first non-empty `session_id`) and correct summary (result > last assistant > last plain line), and does not throw.
Category 6 (skills reach only the Implementer): no finding. `skills` appears only in `ImplementActivityInput` and the Implementer prompt; `buildReviewerInput` and `buildUserValidatorInput` receive no skills field.
Category 7 (three-policy ordering / org skills egress): no finding. Policies are applied create→repo-hosts→hosts+allow-list→allow-list-only, and the org skills checkout runs under policy two and is dropped from policy three; its host is legitimately required for its own checkout.
Category 8 (configuration-driven runner selection): no finding. Selection reads `runtime.implementerRunner`/`validatorRunner`/`reviewerRunner` from `.factoree/config.yaml`; no call site hard-codes a runner name.
Category 9: findings 1 and 2 above; no other unhandled error, off-by-one, race, or unbounded loop found.

Note: the working tree currently holds uncommitted edits to `src/domain/runs/skill-discovery.ts` that change exactly the cap code flagged in Finding 1 (slicing in precedence order before the alphabetical sort). That uncommitted edit is outside the audited range `84a0e9b..HEAD`; Finding 1 stands against HEAD.
